{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or below) as it often signals market cooling or policy tightening.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior day) by applying a dampening factor to avoid overreaction.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% to align with historical volatility patterns.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment when sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.50) — model should anticipate upward momentum.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce volatility in later periods if sentiment remains flat (0.00) — avoid overfitting to recent noise.",
    "When sentiment history shows a recent upward trend (e.g., 0.33, 0.50), model should anticipate sustained price movement and avoid premature corrections.",
    "If forecast consistently underperforms (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below true outcome), apply a bias correction by adding 2-5% to next forecast to compensate for lag."
  ]
}
